title: Composition of regular immersions over arbitrary schemes
statement: Let $i:Z\to Y$ and $j:Y\to X$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Call a morphism $a:T\to W$ a regular immersion if it is an immersion and every point of $T$ has an open neighbourhood $T_0$ for which $a|_{T_0}$ factors as $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq W$, where the last map is an affine open inclusion [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion] and $I$ is generated by a finite $A$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Here an immersion means a closed immersion into an open subscheme, and the empty regular sequence is allowed. If $i$ and $j$ are regular immersions, then $j\circ i$ is a regular immersion. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 067Q (lemma-composition-regular-immersion), assertion (1); affine description from Tags 063G (lemma-regular-ideal-sheaf-scheme) and 063J (definition-regular-immersion).

proof.text: The hypotheses include that $i$ and $j$ are immersions. Clause (e), in its immersion case, of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] therefore shows that $j\circ i$ is an immersion. It remains to construct the regular affine presentation required in the statement at each point $z\in Z$.

Fix $z\in Z$ and put $y=i(z)$ and $x=j(y)$. Unpack the two regular-immersion hypotheses. For $j$ choose an open neighbourhood $Y_0$ of $y$ identified with $\operatorname{Spec}R$, where $R=A/I$, $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$, the $f$ sequence is $A$-regular, and $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is open in $X$. For $i$ choose an open neighbourhood $Z_0$ of $z$ closed in an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $Y$, with $Z_0=\operatorname{Spec}(B/K)$ and $K=(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$ generated by a $B$-regular sequence. In particular $y\in Y_0\cap W$. These are exactly the presentations supplied by the hypotheses; neither $Y_0=j^{-1}(U)$ nor $Z_0=i^{-1}(W)$ is needed.

source.place: Tags 063J (definition-regular-immersion), 063G (lemma-regular-ideal-sheaf-scheme); unpack the affine formulation in the item

proof.text: Construct a common principal neighbourhood without assuming that $Y_0\cap W$ is affine. Apply [lem-sc-affine-inter-principal-both] to the affine opens $Y_0$ and $W$ of $Y$ and the point $y\in Y_0\cap W$: there are $e\in R=\mathcal O_Y(Y_0)$ and $b\in B=\mathcal O_Y(W)$ with $y\in W^{\prime}:=D_{Y_0}(e)=D_W(b)$. Thus $W^{\prime}$ is principal in both $W$ and $Y_0$. Choose a lift $a\in A$ of $e\in R=A/I$ (the map $A\to A/I$ is surjective). By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](a), applied on $U$ and on $Y_0$, the points of $D_{Y_0}(e)$ are the primes $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$ of $A$ with $a\notin\mathfrak p$; hence $W^{\prime}$ is the inverse image in $Y_0$ of the affine open $U^{\prime}=D_U(a)$ under $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\hookrightarrow U$, and $j(W^{\prime})\subseteq U^{\prime}$.

source.place: Tag 01IW (lemma-standard-open-two-affines), stated by lem-sc-affine-inter-principal-both; the lift to A as in Tag 063G

proof.text: Write $A^{\prime}=A_a$ and $R^{\prime}=\Gamma(W^{\prime},\mathcal O_Y)$. The principal-open section comparison gives $R^{\prime}\cong B_b\cong R_{e}\cong A^{\prime}/IA^{\prime}$. The last isomorphism sends the class of $v/a^n$ to $\bar v/e^n$; its inverse sends $\bar v/e^n$ to the class of $v/a^n$, independently of the lift $v$. The same comparison identifies $U^{\prime}$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A^{\prime}$. The localization theorem [lem-exc-weakly-regular-sequence-localization] makes the images $f^{\prime}$ of $f$ weakly regular in $A^{\prime}$ and the images $g^{\prime}$ of $g$ weakly regular in $B_b$. Let $Z^{\prime}=Z_0\cap i^{-1}(W^{\prime})$, an open neighbourhood of $z$ in $Z$. Applied to the closed immersion $Z_0\to W$, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion](1) gives $Z^{\prime}=\operatorname{Spec}C$. More explicitly, the restriction to the basic open $D(b)$ is $C=(B/K)_b=B_b/(g^{\prime})$, by the fraction maps just described. Hence the composite on these charts is the surjection $A^{\prime}\to R^{\prime}=B_b\to C$.

source.place: Tag 067Q (lemma-composition-regular-immersion), affine reduction of (1); affine restriction and localization as in Tag 063G

proof.text: Lift each $g_k^{\prime}\in R^{\prime}$ to $t_k\in A^{\prime}$. The kernel of $A^{\prime}\to C$ is $J=(f_1^{\prime},\ldots,f_r^{\prime},t_1,\ldots,t_s)$: if the image of $v$ is $\sum d_k g_k^{\prime}$, lift the $d_k$ and subtract $\sum \widetilde d_k t_k$ to put $v$ in $IA^{\prime}$. By [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], the concatenated sequence is weakly regular: its first $r$ prefix multiplications are those for $f^{\prime}$; after that, $A^{\prime}/(f^{\prime},t_1,\ldots,t_{k-1})\cong R^{\prime}/(g_1^{\prime},\ldots,g_{k-1}^{\prime})$, and multiplication by $t_k$ is multiplication by $g_k^{\prime}$, which is injective. Its final quotient is $C\ne0$, since $\operatorname{Spec}C$ contains $z$. Thus it is regular, including when either block is empty. The presentation $Z^{\prime}=\operatorname{Spec}(A^{\prime}/J)\hookrightarrow U^{\prime}\subseteq X$ is the required chart for $j\circ i$ at $z$. If $Z$ is empty the chart condition is vacuous; step 1 still supplies the immersion. No finiteness or Noetherian condition on the rings was used.
